decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-20560986 describes a 20-year-old female with a personal history of pheochromocytoma and a malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas, along with a family history of early-onset pheochromocytomas. The proband's mother was identified to have a point mutation (X214L) in exon three of the VHL gene. The title of the paper explicitly states that this mutation is consistent with Type 2A phenotype and low risk of renal cell carcinoma. Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease Type 2A is characterized by pheochromocytoma, retinal capillary hemangioma, and pancreatic lesions (including endocrine tumors), with a low risk of renal cell carcinoma. The evidence supports the association of the VHL *214L (c.641G>T) variant with predisposition to pheochromocytoma and pancreatic endocrine tumors, which are listed phenotypes in the claim. The variant is described as a germline mutation in the family context, supporting the 'predisposition' significance and 'RARE_GERMLINE' origin. The evidence aligns with the claim that this variant predisposes to the specified phenotypes in the context of VHL disease.
